title: How many ways can you give?
headline: There is no one way to give to Watsi. Gift cards, weddings, a student chapter, your time: every one ends in a real patient's care.
story: The question comes first, on screen: how many ways can you give? Kat answers with real people: a family that sent Watsi gift cards instead of Christmas cards, a couple who raised money instead of asking for wedding gifts, a student chapter, a volunteer writer, a monthly gift to the Universal Fund.
It ends on her line: “There isn't really one way to show up. You get to make it your own.” Friendly and light. Not a fundraising ad: no donate button, no urgency.
do: Open on frame 1 with the question typed on screen and Kat already on camera.
Then a straight cut into her answer. Question first, answer second.
Keep captions on the whole time, Lato, large. One text at a time.
Name super “Kat” only, large, after the question has landed.
Write names the way the script doc writes them: Kerney, Reena, Causely, Ronnah.
dont: Don't open on Kat saying hello or on a logo.
Don't use the false starts, “sorry” lines or prompter chat. Only the takes named below.
Don't speed-ramp her voice. Trim breaths and pauses instead.
Don't make Daniel's Stony Brook story the spine. Here it is one example, said once.

voice.quote: One of my favorite things about Watsi is how many different ways people have made giving their own.

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: You can send someone a Watsi gift card instead of another thing they don't need or for the person who has everything. For a birthday, a holiday, a wedding, whatever, the person gets to choose a patient themselves, which makes the gift feel a little more personal.
voice.src: C5051 00:18–00:33 (skip “You can really personalize the experience”)

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: The Kerney family actually turned it into a holiday tradition. Instead of sending Christmas cards once a year, they sent 50 Watsi gift cards to friends and family, and they got their kids involved too.

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: And then there are the people who take one of their own big life moments and turn it into a way to help someone else. Reena and Justin raised money for Watsi instead of asking for wedding gifts. A Watsi supporter named Chris turned a Kilimanjaro climb into a fundraiser. People have done birthdays, hikes, races, all kinds of things. You bring your people together, raise what you can, and then choose patients to support together.

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.
rows.motion: Captions only. At “300 patients …” the transcript writes “in Towning”. The script says “and counting”. Listen and caption what she says.

voice.quote: Students have done this too. Daniel started a Watsi chapter at Stony Brook when he was in college. He got together a group of students, hosted events, and then started raising money. Ten years later, that chapter is still going strong and they have now helped 300 patients … get the care that they need. That was one of my favorite Watsi stories because it started with one student, one idea, and getting a bunch of people together.
voice.src: C5051 02:44–03:06 (the clean take; the 01:30 take says “30 or 300”)

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: You can also give your time. People have volunteered as Watsi writers helping bring patient stories to the site. Ravi started that way, writing more than 60 patient profiles, and later became a Universal Fund donor. For some people, the thing that they give Watsi first isn't money. It's a few hours, a skill, or a bit of time.

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: You can give every month through the Universal Fund. … So yes, donating is the simplest way to get involved, but you can also give. You can give at your birthday, your wedding, your workplace. You can give your creativity, your time, or your people.

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: That's one thing I love about Watsi. There isn't really one way to show up. You get to make it your own.
